variables.reason: The typed ledger labels Ra as the first-order absolute moment of height fluctuations (mean absolute deviation). The KB record pq_arithmetic_mean_roughness explicitly defines the arithmetic mean roughness (symbols Ra; R_a; aliases: first-order moment of height fluctuations) and gives si_dimension: L, confirming this quantity is a length. The entry therefore directly describes the same physical quantity named Ra in the original problem and supports every nonzero/zero coordinate in the proposed SI exponent vector (length exponent = 1, all other base exponents = 0).

The ledger defines kt as peak-to-valley height. The KB record pq_peak_to_valley_height denotes mean peak-to-valley roughness height with symbols including k_t and kt, explicitly describes it as a roughness amplitude formed from vertical height differences and assigns si_dimension: L. This entry applies to the same physical measure (a vertical distance) used in the original problem and therefore supports the proposed SI exponent vector (L=1, others zero).

The typed ledger gives k_rms as RMS height of surface roughness. The KB record pq_rms_roughness_height defines root-mean-square roughness height (symbols k_rms; krms) and assigns si_dimension: L, explicitly matching the physical meaning (an RMS vertical distance). Therefore this record directly supports the candidate SI exponent vector (only L nonzero).

The ledger names Sk as skewness of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_skewness describes surface-height skewness (symbol Sk) as the third standardized moment of the height distribution and gives si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This is the same statistical measure in the original problem, so the record supports all coordinates of the proposed SI vector (all zeros).

The ledger lists Ku as kurtosis of height fluctuations. The KB record pq_height_kurtosis defines surface-height kurtosis (symbol Ku) as the fourth standardized moment and reports si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). This entry is the canonical definition of the same statistical quantity in the problem and therefore supports the proposed all-zero SI exponent vector for Ku.

The ledger defines ES as effective streamwise slope (mean absolute surface gradient). The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope names effective surface slope (symbols ES) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record directly corresponds to the ES variable in the problem and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The ledger gives Po as surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po; P_o; phi_p) as a fraction or void fraction and assigns si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The entry applies to the same geometric fraction called Po in the problem, and it supports the proposed SI exponent vector (all zeros).

candidate_ledger.output_variable_reasoning: ks/Ra is the normalized equivalent sand-grain roughness (ratio of two lengths) and is therefore dimensionless. The seven provided inputs include three quantities with dimensions of length (Ra, kt, k_rms) and four dimensionless shape/geometry descriptors (Sk, Ku, ES, Po). Dimensional analysis therefore yields that ks/Ra can only depend on dimensionless combinations formed from these inputs, e.g. kt/Ra and k_rms/Ra and the purely dimensionless descriptors Sk, Ku, ES, Po. Confidence is high because the physical meanings are standard and the dimensional roles (length vs. dimensionless) are unambiguous.

This is the same statistical measure in the original problem, so the record supports all coordinates of the proposed SI vector (all zeros).

This entry is the canonical definition of the same statistical quantity in the problem and therefore supports the proposed all-zero SI exponent vector for Ku.

The KB record pq_effective_surface_slope names effective surface slope (symbols ES) as the mean absolute gradient of surface height in a horizontal direction and explicitly states that a surface-height derivative is length divided by length and therefore dimensionless (si_dimension: 1). This record directly corresponds to the ES variable in the problem and supports the all-zero SI exponent vector.

The ledger gives Po as surface porosity. The KB record pq_porosity defines porosity (symbols Po; P_o; phi_p) as a fraction or void fraction and assigns si_dimension: 1 (dimensionless). The entry applies to the same geometric fraction called Po in the problem, and it supports the proposed SI exponent vector (all zeros).

variables.physical_definition: First-order absolute moment of height fluctuations (mean absolute deviation of surface height).
Peak-to-valley height of the surface (maximum vertical distance between peak and valley).
Root-mean-square (RMS) height of the surface roughness (square-root of mean squared height).
Skewness of the roughness height fluctuations (third standardized moment of height distribution).
Kurtosis of the roughness height fluctuations (fourth standardized moment of height distribution).
Effective streamwise slope of the roughness (dimensionless slope measure of surface features).
Surface porosity (fraction of surface area that is void).
